title: Remove fish scales without cutting the skin
instruction: Remove the remaining scales from the exposed side of the fish with the scaler, without cutting its skin. Leave the fish on the board and release it.
context: Descaling needs firm support and tail-to-head scraping against overlapping scales, with enough pressure to lift scales without damaging the skin.
setup: A 260 mm, approximately 250 g prepared whole fish lies on a fixed 250 x 300 x 8 mm wooden board. Its underside is already descaled; 26 equal-area scaled sectors remain on the exposed side. A loose 87 g stainless scaler with a 56 x 50 mm serrated head lies clear of the board. Two 40 x 6 x 1 mm precision finger extensions per arm have a 4 N jaw limit. The starting layout is fixed; no fish or tool is attached to the board.
scoring: After 3 seconds with open fingers at least 65 mm clear, score the fraction of the 26 initially scaled sectors left free of scales. Zero if the skin is torn or crushed, the fish is no longer supported upright on its prepared side on the board, or the robot has not released it. Photographs with a ruler support before/after area and damage checks.
fidelity: A rigid fish body, including its tail, carries compliant skin and 26 retained scale groups. Loaded tail-to-head tool contact releases groups; excess skin compression or broken skin joints loses credit. This approximates scraping and damage, not flesh deformation, tail tearing or microscopic scale mechanics. Contact-checked, force-limited pinch joints approximate finger friction.
reset_notes: Use a fresh prepared fish with its underside descaled and its exposed side scaled. Remove loose scales from the board and scaler before resetting. Fixed layout; no object jitter.
